concept_name: Will the calendar for 2025 ever be used again, and when?

item.question: Will the calendar for 2025 (an ordinary year) be reused, and when?
steps: 2025 to 2026: shift 1 (total 1).
2026 to 2027: shift 1 (total 2).
2027 to 2028: shift 1 (total 3).
2028 is a leap year, so 2028 to 2029: shift 2 (total 5).
2029 to 2030: shift 1 (total 6).
2030 to 2031: shift 1 (total 7), a whole week, and 2031 is ordinary.
item.answer: Yes: 2031 uses exactly the same calendar as 2025.
item.text:
Example 2: Will the calendar for 2025 (an ordinary year) be reused, and when?
1. 2025 to 2026: shift 1 (total 1).
2. 2026 to 2027: shift 1 (total 2).
3. 2027 to 2028: shift 1 (total 3).
4. 2028 is a leap year, so 2028 to 2029: shift 2 (total 5).
5. 2029 to 2030: shift 1 (total 6).
6. 2030 to 2031: shift 1 (total 7), a whole week, and 2031 is ordinary.
Answer: Yes: 2031 uses exactly the same calendar as 2025.

item.question: Gandhinagar to Kohima: about how many kilometres?
steps_tex: Sample answer: estimate from the map of India, because the two towns are nearly at opposite ends.
India is about $3000\text{ km}$ wide from west to east.
Gandhinagar is a little in from the western edge and Kohima a little in from the eastern edge.
Take off about $250\text{ km}$ at each end: $3000 - 250 - 250 = 2500\text{ km}$.
Taking off $400\text{ km}$ at each end gives $3000 - 400 - 400 = 2200\text{ km}$, so the estimate lies between about $2200$ and $2500\text{ km}$.
